first_hunter_context.positioning_check: FINRA short interest at the 2026-10-15 settlement was 7,056,099 shares, up 391,203 on the prior period: 2.0% of ~361.8M shares outstanding, 2.53 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/el/shortinterest). Not a crowded short and no squeeze mechanism. evidence.text: L'Oreal's Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep, the same months as EL's fiscal Q1) beat: group LFL +7.7% against 5.9% expected. Travel retail returned to growth with sell-in +10% and sell-out up low to mid single digits. Hainan was 'very positive', North Asia TR was less negative (-MSD), China domestic beauty was about +2-3%, and the CEO put global beauty at ~+5%. That supports EL's guided H1 driver of 'stronger travel retail shipments' (TR ~15% of EL sales), which consensus has at about +4.9% reported growth.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Travel retail and China have driven EL's biggest reactions: 2025-02-04 -16.07% and 2026-02-05 -19.19% (baseline), versus +16.3% on 2026-08-19, when management said TR turned positive in June/July led by Hainan (Q4 FY26 transcript).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. L'Oreal reported on 2026-10-22, EL closed $108.67 on 10-23 (+0.88%) and has drifted to $106.69. If the TR read-through were fully priced, the 5-day run-up would be positive and the skew more call-bid than -1.7. The ~+5% revenue consensus sits at the middle of the FY organic range even though management said H1 runs ahead of H2. The finding is shrunk because it lands inside a guided H1 driver and covers one segment of ~15% of sales, with the other ~85% (NA, EUKEM, China mainland) needing to hold.
evidence.independence: Separate sources: L'Oreal group/North Asia +7.8% and TR 'sustained growth' (Luxury Tribune, https://www.luxurytribune.com/en/loreal-accelerates-growth-in-the-3rd-quarter-of-2026-driven-by-luxury-and-emerging-markets, 2026-10-23); Hainan offshore duty-free H1 2026 +18.8% y/y per Haikou Customs (https://m.gelonghui.com/live/2443334, cited in search); Korea duty-free +15.9% in July (filed separately below). Same direction, different series.

evidence.text: Korea duty-free sales (excluding inflight) rose 15.9% y/y in July 2026 to KRW1.067tn, driven by foreigners (77.3% of sales; airport foreign sales +22.7%, downtown +30.3%). Korea TR was a named driver of EL's FY26 Asia/Pacific growth, and July is EL's fiscal Q1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same TR line as above; no EL-specific reaction to Korean duty-free data on record.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is an industry series that sell-side TR models read loosely. One month of data, out two months before the print. It is a proxy, not EL's sell-in, and Korean nationals' purchases fell 13.5%. Small.
evidence.independence: Proxy. Independent of the L'Oreal call. EL's FY26 release names Korea and Hong Kong TR and Hainan as APAC drivers (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001250/000100125026000038/elq4fy2026exhibit991.htm).

evidence.text: China's NBS cosmetics retail sales rose 5.4% y/y in September 2026 to RMB39.0bn and 6.1% for Jan-Sep, while total retail grew only 1.1% (gold/jewellery -9.6%). Cosmetics held up in a weak consumer tape during EL's fiscal Q1. EL's mainland China grew high single digits in FY26 (+7% organic in Q4).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: China has been the swing line in EL's large moves (2025-02-04 -16.07%, 2026-02-05 -19.19%). Q4 FY26 China +7% organic coincided with +16.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a public macro series, so largely priced. It mixes mass and prestige and is not EL's own number. It is filed small as confirmation that the China trend did not break during the quarter. EL's China investor event on Nov 4 means management will want to show China strength.
evidence.independence: L'Oreal's CEO put China domestic beauty at about +2-3% for nine months, a weaker figure (https://moodiedavittreport.com/?p=486532). Puig's Asia Pacific grew +12.9% LFL in Q3 (https://moodiedavittreport.com/?p=486411).

evidence.text: Puig's Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep): group LFL +5.6%. Skincare fell 0.8% at constant perimeter, its second straight negative quarter, and management said premium skincare 'remained soft'. Makeup grew +16.1%. EL is the most skin-care-weighted prestige house (Estee Lauder, Clinique, La Mer), so the read is negative for its largest category and positive for MAC/Clinique makeup, which EL guided to return to growth.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean EL reaction to a skin-care-only surprise in the baseline. Skin care weakness was part of the FY25 sell-offs.
evidence.why_not_priced: Peer category data is read by the beauty analysts, so mostly priced. Filed net of the offsetting makeup strength. Circana's H1 2026 US prestige skincare +9% contradicts a broad skincare slump, so this is sized below that series.
evidence.independence: Puig's skincare is small (~10% of sales) and partly dermocosmetics. Circana US prestige H1 2026: skincare +9%, makeup +3%, fragrance +6% (https://www.premiumbeautynews.com/en/us-beauty-market-stays-strong-in,28150) points the other way.

evidence.text: LVMH Perfumes & Cosmetics (Dior, Guerlain, Givenchy) grew only ~1% organically in Q3 2026 and was flat over nine months, citing a less buoyant China. Selective Retailing (Sephora) grew +8% organically with share gains. Prestige brand owners other than L'Oreal were soft while the retailer was strong.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Peer softness in China preceded EL's 2025-02 and 2026-02 drops.
evidence.why_not_priced: Released 2026-10-12, before EL's October run toward $108.7, so the market looked through it. It is the counterweight to the L'Oreal read and shows the prestige read-through is not uniform.
evidence.independence: Contradicted in part by L'Oreal Luxe +7% (https://www.luxurytribune.com/en/loreal-accelerates-growth-in-the-3rd-quarter-of-2026-driven-by-luxury-and-emerging-markets). Separate document.

evidence.text: Amazon Prime Day 2026 ran June 23-26, in EL's fiscal Q4 FY26. In 2025 it ran in July, inside fiscal Q1 FY26. So Q1 FY27 laps a Prime Day quarter with no event of its own, and Amazon sell-in moved into Q4. Management flagged the shift on the August call but also said July retail in North America was 'extremely strong', led by Clinique and MAC. Net: a modest North America timing headwind against a strong July.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: North America returned to organic growth only in Q4 FY26 (Americas +5% organic), on the print that rose +16.3%. Earnings Whispers names NA sustainability as a key watch point.
evidence.why_not_priced: Management mentioned it on the call, so models likely carry some timing. If the market had weighted it, previews would discount the Q1 NA number; the Earnings Whispers preview names NA as a watch point without the timing. Sized small and netted against the 'July extremely strong' comment.
evidence.independence: Same management commentary as the July-strength statement: Q4 FY26 transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/EL/Q42026), one document, so merged into one finding. Prime Day dates are independently confirmed (https://thenextweb.com/news/amazon-moves-prime-day-back-to-june-and-keeps-it-a-four-day-event).

evidence.text: The setup carries a raised bar. Shares are up ~16% since the August print (+16.0% over 20 days), near the post-earnings high ($109.35) and well above the 200-day ($91.76). The whisper is $0.60 against a $0.50-0.53 consensus, and bullish sentiment rose to 19.2% from 6.5%. A beat at consensus likely clears less than an in-line guide reiteration costs.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 (2025-10-30), a reaffirm after a strong pre-print run, moved +0.26%. Q4 FY25 (2025-08-20) -3.67% and Q3 FY25 -1.78% on in-line prints. Beats with raised guides have paid (+16.3%), misses on China/TR have cost 16-19%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself, so this is not 'unpriced'. It is filed as the bar the print has to clear. Against it: short interest is only 2.0% with 2.5 days to cover, and the skew (-1.7) leans slightly to calls, which is why this is sized small.
evidence.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_20d +16.0%, pct_from_52w_high -10.8%). Short interest rose 391k shares into 2026-10-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/el/shortinterest).

evidence.text: Interparfums' Q3 2026 USD sales were flat at ~$430M. US-based operations fell 7%, mainly on delayed giftset shipments, while Coach rose 23% and Montblanc 12%. The CEO said activity improved over the summer and the company targets the top of FY guidance. This is a soft read on US fragrance sell-in timing for the holiday build.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No EL history on this line. Fragrance is EL's growth category (Le Labo, Tom Ford, Kilian, Jo Malone), but Interparfums is masstige/licensed.
evidence.why_not_priced: Off-line peer (masstige licences), widely reported. The decline is a giftset timing issue, not demand. Tiny.
evidence.independence: Puig Fragrance & Fashion +3.9% LFL in Q3 (https://moodiedavittreport.com/?p=486411) and L'Oreal naming fragrance its strongest category point the other way.

evidence.text: Q4 FY26 adjusted EPS included a $38M (+$0.07) benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds booked in cost of sales. The FY26 10-K says remaining unsubmitted or unreceived refunds are 'not material', so Q1 FY27 should carry no comparable refund. There is no hidden one-off upside to the $0.50-0.53 bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The refund sat inside the +16.3% Q4 print, which traded on guidance, not on the refund.
evidence.why_not_priced: Disclosed in the 10-K and immaterial by the company's own statement. Filed to close off the refund angle that moved other names; sized 0.
evidence.independence: Q4 FY26 release states the $38M benefit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001250/000100125026000038/elq4fy2026exhibit991.htm). Same company, different document.

first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 EPS consensus $3.70-3.71 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-10-26 https://finviz.com/news/407882/idexx-must-show-new-cancer-tests-can-outrun-soft-vet-visits-in-q3 ; KeyCorp $3.70 https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/estimates-what-is-keycorps-estimate-for-idxx-q3-earnings-2026-10-14/ ; Benzinga $3.70 https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IDXX/earnings-forecasts), whisper $3.82; Q3 revenue consensus ~$1.19B (+8% vs ~$1.11B; one source, Earnings Whispers). Company guide (Q2 call 2026-08-04, https://www.webull.com/news/15344824561263616): Q3 organic growth in line with the implied H2 range, Q3 reported operating margin 32.5-32.8%, Q3 FX ~70bp headwind to reported revenue; FY2026 revenue $4,700-4,745M, organic 8.5-9.7%, CAG recurring organic 9.5-10.7%, EPS $14.69-14.94, H2 US clinical visits ~-1.5% (8-K ex99.1 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000874716/000110465926090033/tm2622041d1_ex99-1.htm). My arithmetic: H1 2026 revenue $2,357M at 10.0% organic implies H2 organic ~7.1-9.4% (midpoint ~8.2%); the $1.19B consensus at +~7.7% reported plus ~0.7pt FX is ~8.4% organic, i.e. slightly above the guided midpoint. FY EPS consensus reported at $14.68, below the guide low end (single AI-generated source, treated as disputed).
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 1,929,268 shares, 2.47% of float, 3.6 days to cover, settlement 2026-10-15, published by FINRA 2026-10-26, down 0.6% vs prior (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/IDXX/short-interest/). Not crowded, no squeeze mechanism. Baseline: 25d skew +0.49 vol points (balanced, priced_direction_lean 'balanced'), event-implied move 8.06%, put/call OI 2.23 on only 681 contracts total (too thin to read), run-up +8.44% over 20 sessions and +0.31% over 5, spot 562.13 is -26.7% from the 52-week high and +11.4% from the low.

evidence.text: Vetsource data (CATalyst Council release 2026-10-13, reported by dvm360 2026-10-23, 6,595 US practices) show all-species US clinical visits down 1.9% YoY in Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep), canine down and puppy visits -10%, feline +2.7%; management's H2 assumption on the Q2 call was ~-1.5% US clinical visits after a -1.3% Q2 on IDEXX's own same-store measure, so this industry series sits ~0.4pt worse than the planning assumption.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Visits are the line this name has traded on in 2026: the Q4 2025 print (2026-02-02) beat and guided above estimates but the stock fell -4.6% on a cautious ~-2% visits assumption; Q2 (2026-08-04) reported -1.3% visits with a 10% organic recurring beat and the stock rose +3.6%. A visits headwind has been absorbed by price (~4%) and test intensity in every 2026 quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a trade-press series rather than a wire item, and IDEXX measures visits on its own panel with a different definition, so the street's -1.5% assumption is the company's; if the -1.9% were priced, Q3 revenue consensus would sit at or below the guided H2 midpoint rather than slightly above it (~8.4% organic vs ~8.2%), and the 20-day run-up of +8.4% into the print argues the market is not leaning on visit weakness. Caveat sized in: Vetsource and IDEXX's panel differ, the Q2 Vetsource comparable is not cleanly sourced (the July release gives -1.50% for the twelve months to June), and feline growth (+2.7%) favours diagnostic intensity.
evidence.independence: Management's own H2 assumption on the Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/idexx-laboratories-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-04/) is the comparison, not corroboration. Merck Animal Health's Q3 companion animal +6% ex-FX (finding 2) is a different, product-driven series and neither confirms nor contradicts visits. Proxy: macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by IDEXX.

evidence.text: Merck's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-29), the only vet-channel counterparty to report since IDEXX last spoke, shows companion animal sales $628M, +6% ex-FX, 'largely driven by new product launches', with Bravecto flat ex-FX, after +7% in Q2 and +9% in Q1 2026: a vet-channel read that is steady-to-slightly-decelerating and silent on visits.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved instance of IDXX reacting to a Merck Animal Health read; the name's prints are driven by its own CAG recurring growth and guidance (+14.8% Nov 2025, +27.5% Aug 2025 on raises).
evidence.why_not_priced: Published three sessions before the print inside a $17bn pharma release; Animal Health is a small line nobody previews IDEXX on. If it had been read as a vet-channel slowdown, animal-health names would have sold off on 2026-10-29/30; the baseline 5-day run-up of +0.3% shows no such move in IDXX. It is a weak, product-mix-driven proxy for an IDEXX diagnostics quarter, so small.
evidence.independence: Different source from finding 1 (Vetsource) and points weakly the same way (deceleration from +9% to +7% to +6%). Zoetis reports 2026-11-05, after the window (https://investor.zoetis.com/news/news-details/2026/Zoetis-to-Host-Webcast-and-Conference-Call-on-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx).

evidence.text: The dollar has strengthened since IDEXX set its FY guide on 2026-08-04: DXY ~100.3-100.8 at end-July (Cambridge Currencies / Convex estimates) against 101.81-101.87 on 2026-10-23/26 (RTTNews), roughly 1-1.5%; IDEXX's stated sensitivity is ~$8M of revenue per 1% stronger dollar for the rest of the year, so the reported FY revenue guide carries an ~$8-12M FX cut (about 0.2%), the same mechanism that took $15M off the guide in August.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-04 an organic raise was netted by a $15M FX cut, leaving the revenue midpoint +$5M; the stock rose +3.6% on the EPS raise. FX-driven trims have not been the deciding line in the 2026 reactions.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street usually updates FX in models, so this is likely partly priced; what is not priced is the headline optics: if the organic beat is ~$10M the reported revenue range may not rise at all, which is what a headline-driven open reacts to. If priced, revenue consensus ($1.19B) would sit at or below the guided midpoint rather than slightly above it. Small because ~0.2% of revenue and partly offsettable by margin.
evidence.independence: Sensitivity from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15344824561263616); end-July DXY from https://cambridgecurrencies.com/us-dollar-index-dxy-forecast/ (estimate, not an ICE close). Independent of findings 1 and 2.

evidence.text: The FY2026 EPS consensus is reported at $14.68, one cent below the low end of IDEXX's own raised guide of $14.69-14.94 (and ~$0.13 below its midpoint), while the Q3 EPS whisper is $3.82 against a $3.71 consensus; a reaffirmed or raised EPS range therefore lands above the street's full-year number.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS-guide raises bought +3.6% (Aug 2026), 0.0% (May 2026), +14.8% (Nov 2025) and +27.5% (Aug 2025); the 2026 reactions to raises have been muted.
evidence.why_not_priced: A consensus below the company's own floor means the sell-side is haircutting the guide (FX, H2 spend); if the market fully trusted the guide the consensus would sit at the midpoint. Capped small: the $14.68 figure has one source, an AI-generated preview, and the whisper shows the buy-side already expects a beat.
evidence.independence: Guide range from the company 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000874716/000110465926090033/tm2622041d1_ex99-1.htm). The FX finding (3) argues the haircut is partly justified; net of it this stays small.

evidence.text: Product cadence inside Q3 that feeds recurring revenue: Cancer Dx expanded in late September to a panel adding mast cell tumor detection at no price increase, with >20% of Cancer Dx orders from practices using a competitor's reference lab; inVue Dx FNA rollout began in Q3 toward broad availability by year-end (management: roughly doubles procedure volume for users); company on pace for 5,500 inVue placements in 2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Innovation-driven recurring beats have been sold or ignored in 2026 (0.0% in May, -4.6% in Feb despite beats); they paid in 2025 (+27.5%, +14.8%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are company-disclosed and flagged in previews. What is not yet visible is the Q3 number (Cancer Dx clinic count, FNA uptake, competitive-lab wins); if the market credited it, recurring growth expectations would sit above the 9.5-10.7% guided range rather than inside it. Small, and inside what the company already guided.
evidence.independence: Morgan Stanley conference summary 2026-09-14 (https://quartr.com/events/idexx-laboratories-idxx-morgan-stanley-24th-annual-global-healthcare-conference_3YkDXwfA) repeats the FNA and Cancer Dx points: same company, so one source.

evidence.text: The stock ran from ~$518-520 on 2026-10-06/09 (Wealth Awesome, Bloomberg Línea) to $562.13 at the seal (+8.4% in 20 sessions, baseline), into a print where the 2026 beat-and-raise quarters bought 0.0% and +3.6% and the guide-led Q4 bought -4.6%; the run-up raises the bar for the reaction while short interest (2.47% of float, 3.6 days) offers no squeeze cushion.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 2026 reactions +3.57, -0.03, -4.60 against 2025's +14.84, +27.49, +8.95, +11.13; the name's response to good numbers has damped as the stock de-rated.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself price, so this is the bar rather than a mispricing; it is filed because a beat now has to clear an extra ~8% of anticipation. If the market were pricing disappointment, skew would be bid (it is +0.49, balanced) and the stock would not have recovered off the low. Sized small: the stock is still 27% off its high and the run-up may be valuation repair rather than earnings anticipation.
evidence.independence: Spot and run-up from the sealed baseline; Oct 9 quote https://www.bloomberglinea.com/quote/IDXX:UN/ ; short interest https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/IDXX/short-interest/ .

evidence.text: The Q3 revenue bar of about $126.5M is +6.1% on Q2's $119.2M, but in the same quarter last year Vyjuvek grew only +1.9% q/q ($96.0M to $97.8M), and management then cited summer therapy pauses and 'a bit lower' US sales. That year's consensus had modelled a q/q decline ($93.7M against $96.0M), and the quarter beat by 4.4%. This year's consensus assumes no summer dip on a US base of $91.6M, so a repeat of the seasonal pattern lands the quarter around $121-124M, a 2-4% miss.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue misses: Q1 2025 -10.6% on revenue gave -14.06% (2025-05-06); Q2 2026 -1.4% on revenue gave -8.37% (2026-08-03). Beats: Q3 2025 +4.4% gave +0.17%; Q4 2025 +1.7% gave +4.12%. Revenue misses are sold hard and beats bought mildly.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at +6% q/q, and higher at Benzinga and Chartmill, shows the street is not modelling a summer dip this year, unlike last year when it modelled a q/q decline. If the seasonal risk were priced, Q3 estimates would sit at or below Q2's $119-122M. The puts are bid only modestly (+4 vol points), and the stock is up 5% in five days into the print.
evidence.independence: Q3 2025 consensus and actuals from a separate source: https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/krys. evidence.text: Germany's AMNOG price negotiation for Vyjuvek should conclude around the Q3 print. The G-BA decision came on 2026-02-19 (procedure start 2025-08-15), so the six-month negotiation ran to about 2026-08-19. On the Q2 call management said it expected completion in Q3 and called its accrual 'conservative'. A full quarter of German price reserve had kept Q2 ex-US revenue flat at $27.6M (vs $28.9M in Q1), with 'maybe a partial' reserve in Q3 and normal German net revenue by Q4. The outcome, a final price at or above the accrual (reserve release, clean ex-US run-rate) or arbitration by the Schiedsstelle (overhang persists), is likely disclosed in the Q3 release.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: ex-US revenue went flat on the German reserve and total revenue missed by 1.4%; the stock fell 8.37% on 2026-08-03. No earlier price-resolution event to compare against.
evidence.why_not_priced: No German Erstattungsbetrag or Schiedsstelle decision has been published in any source found, and the 2026-10-28 Trefis note still lists the German negotiation as an open factor. A priced release would show up as Q3 estimates above $130M, or the stock recovering its August loss before the print. Consensus at $126.5M (+$7M q/q) does not clearly embed a catch-up.
evidence.independence: G-BA procedure page confirming the decision date of 2026-02-19 and the procedure start of 2025-08-15: https://www.g-ba.de/bewertungsverfahren/nutzenbewertung/1250/. Q1 ex-US $28.9M: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001711279/000171127926000044/a1q26exhibit991pr.htm. Trefis 2026-10-28 also lists it as unresolved: https://www.trefis.com/stock/krys/articles/620966/has-the-story-under-krystal-biotech-stock-run-out/2026-10-28. This finding partly offsets finding 1 on total revenue; they are separate drivers (US seasonality vs the ex-US reserve).

evidence.text: Q3 2026 was a benign catastrophe quarter by the industry's own counts. Gallagher Re puts 9M26 global insured cat losses at $92bn, the lowest since 2019, with no single event over $10bn and a slow Atlantic season. Hurricane Isaias landed 9 Oct, outside Q3. CNA's Q2 2026 had $60M of pretax cats (2.3 pts) and the CNA bar ($1.19-1.23) is roughly a repeat of Q2's $1.19, so a light Q3 cat load leans toward meeting or beating that bar. Against Q3 2025's very low $41M, though, peers' cats rose year on year (Travelers $538M vs $302M; W.R. Berkley ~$86M vs ~$79M), mainly from severe convective storms.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loews has not traded on CNA cat lines: Q3 2025 (CNA core record $1.50, cats $41M) moved -0.14% on 2025-11-03; Q2 2026 moved +0.21% (baseline).
evidence.why_not_priced: The CNA bar has sat at $1.19-1.23 since a Zacks cut in mid-August and was not raised after the benign-quarter data. If the light cat quarter were priced, CNA estimates would have moved up after Gallagher's 21 Oct report and Travelers' 16 Oct print; no revision was found. The effect is still small, because cats are a minor line for CNA.
evidence.independence: Travelers Q3 2026 8-K: cats $538M, mostly wind/hail, combined ratio 86.8% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000086312/000008631226000180/a991pressrelease93026.htm). W.R. Berkley Q3 cats ~$85.9M vs ~$78.5M (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/10/20/889600.htm). Both are proxies, not CNA's own number.

evidence.text: Commercial middle-market loss trends worsened at peers in Q3 2026, and that is CNA's core book. Hartford's Middle & Large Business underlying combined ratio was 99.5, against 91.4 a year earlier and 95.3 in Q2 2026, on workers' comp and non-cat property; the trade press reported it on 2026-10-27 as a trend, not a one-off. Chubb's North America commercial combined ratio worsened to 86.3 from 81.5, with $13M of unfavorable long-tail development. CNA already raised its 2026 underlying loss picks in Q2 (underlying combined ratio 94.2 vs 91.7), so further deterioration would come on top of that.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loews's largest move in the baseline, -5.86% on 2026-05-04, came when CNA's combined ratio rose to 102.2% on a $106M reserve charge plus a 2.6-pt underlying loss-ratio increase (https://rallies.ai/news/loews-drops-after-q1-profit-declines-as-cna-reserve-charge-hits-underwriting-results). Q2 2026 brought a 2.5-pt underlying increase with no PYD, and the stock moved +0.21%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Hartford spoke on 26-27 Oct, after CNA and Loews last spoke (3 Aug), and the CNA bar ($1.19-1.23) was set before that. If the market had priced it, CNA estimates would have been trimmed in late October, or Loews would have lagged the insurance group in the last week; Loews is flat over 5 days (-0.16%). The read-across is weakened by two peers: Selective booked zero casualty PYD and Chubb's long-tail adverse was only $13M.
evidence.independence: Chubb Q3 2026: NA commercial combined ratio 86.3 vs 81.5, long-tail unfavorable $13M (https://www.reinsurancene.ws/chubb-posts-record-5-79bn-pc-underwriting-income-for-first-nine-months-of-2026/). Against it, Selective had zero prior-year casualty development in Q3 2026 (https://actuary.info/insights/selective-q3-2026-zero-prior-year-casualty-development-cat-losses-5-4-points-npw-down-7-percent) and Hartford's overall PYD was favorable at $61M. Proxy only; CNA has not confirmed.

evidence.text: Q3 is when CNA books its annual Life & Group reserve review, a one-off inside the print. The last two were small: Q3 2025 LTC assumption update +$7M pretax to reserves (about $7M after-tax hit to core per the release), and Q3 2024 +$15M pretax. CNA also did a $1bn LTC portfolio trade in Q2 2026 that extended duration. Nothing points to a large Q3 2026 update, but this is the one scheduled reserve event in the quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (LTC update ~$7M) moved -0.14%; Q3 2024's update was $15M pretax. Neither shows a reaction attributable to the review.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is unquantified until the release. If the market expected a large LTC charge, CNA estimates would sit below the $1.19 Q2 run-rate rather than at or above it. The size is near zero because the history is small; the range carries the tail.
evidence.independence: The CNA Q3 2025 10-Q gives the same $7M pretax update and Q3 2024 at $15M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21175/000002117525000097/cna-20250930.htm), so it shares a source family. The Loews Q2 2026 earnings remarks describe the $1bn LTC portfolio trade (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000060086/000006008626000045/exhibit992-q22026.htm).

evidence.text: Loews Hotels faces a weaker Q3 at its biggest market. Comcast reported on 2026-10-22 that Theme Parks Q3 2026 revenue fell 4.4% to $2,597M and Adjusted EBITDA fell 17.1% to $780M, on lower admissions and more promotions, and said Orlando softness would continue into Q4 and 1H27. Loews Hotels' Universal Orlando JV hotels drove its Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA up 26% to $137M. The Q3 2025 comparison is $69M Adjusted EBITDA (+8%), and the three new Orlando hotels are no longer an incremental year-on-year driver. Net of the rest of the company: hotels are about $69M of EBITDA in a quarter where CNA plus Boardwalk earn about $400M after tax to Loews, so even a 20% hotel miss is roughly $0.05 a share.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hotels have never been the reaction line. Q1 2026 hotels Adjusted EBITDA +53% came with a -5.86% move driven by CNA; Q2 2026 hotels +26% came with +0.21%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Comcast is a counterparty that spoke after Loews last did (3 Aug), and Loews has almost no sell-side coverage to carry the read-across. In the Q2 remarks Loews said there was 'still ramp ahead' and made no mention of softness. The finding stays small because the segment is small.
evidence.independence: Comcast's Q2 2026 call said Orlando attendance softened from June and stayed pressured into Q3 (https://blogmickey.com/2026/07/universal-confirms-orlando-tourism-summer-softness-attendance-below-expectations/, 2026-07-23). That is the same company, so it is not fully independent. Loews Q3 2025 hotels base of $69M: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60086/000006008625000177/exhibit991-q32025.htm.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 equity returns were weak outside mega-caps: S&P 500 total return +2.3% but equal-weight -1.87% (Morgan Stanley), against a very strong Q3 2025. That leans against CNA's limited-partnership and common-stock income, which was $131M in Q2 2026 and $71M in Q3 2025, and against the parent's trading portfolio. Loews's Q3 2025 corporate segment earned $42M, already down on lower trading income, and the parent's trading fixed maturities shrank to $291M at 2026-06-30 from $633M at year end, so the parent leg is smaller now.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Investment-income swings have not been isolated as a reaction line. Q3 2025 (record CNA core, corporate down) moved -0.14%.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company inference. CNA's LP accounting may run on a lag, and the cap-weighted index was positive. It is small and unconfirmed by the company.
evidence.independence: First Trust gives a Q3 2026 S&P 500 total return of 2.3% (https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/10/22/sp-500-index-through-q3-2026). evidence.text: Three peers that reported after Marriott's last update (2026-08-03) printed Q3 RevPAR far above Marriott's own Q3 global guide of +3.5% to +4.0%. Hilton system +5.8% with US +7.0%, Europe +6.5% and MEA -5.6% (8-K, 2026-10-27). That implies Marriott Q3 global RevPAR of roughly +5%, about 1.25pt above the top of its guide, and a mechanical FY RevPAR raise from 3.0-3.5% to about 3.75-4.25%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-03 Marriott beat EPS ($3.19 vs ~$3.05) and raised FY RevPAR, and the stock fell -6.97% on a revenue miss. evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. MAR rose about 2.3% from Oct 27 to Oct 30 and is 0.7% off its high. But the published Street EPS ($2.83-2.88 on most sources) sits barely above the top of the company's $2.74-2.82 guide, which is what a model with Q3 RevPAR near 4% gives. If the Street had moved to +5% RevPAR, consensus would read about $2.92-2.97 rather than $2.86. Only the whisper ($2.92) gets there.
evidence.independence: Three separate primary documents point the same way: Hilton 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001585689/000158568926000049/q32026earningsrelease.htm , IHG Q3 trading update https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2026/third-quarter-trading-update-to-30-september-2026 , and CoStar's segment commentary via https://capitalanalyticsassociates.com/luxury-hotels-emerge-as-bright-spots-in-uneven-us-market/ . All are proxies for Marriott, not Marriott's own number.

evidence.text: The Q4/FY guide is exposed to the Middle East in its peak quarter and to the midterms. Marriott said on its Q2 call that Q4 is normally about 35% of its Middle East full-year revenue, that Q4 2025 had big ADR-lifting events, and that Q4 RevPAR would be 'a bit lower than Q3'. Hilton (2026-10-27) guided Q4 RevPAR to only +3.0-3.5%, flagged an 'increased impact from the Middle East' and cut its FY EBITDA expectation for the Middle East and timeshare fees despite raising RevPAR, and its stock fell 2.1% that day. Accor said UAE RevPAR was still about -20% year on year in Q3 (2026-10-22). Marriott has the largest Gulf footprint of the US majors, so a Q4 fee/EBITDA guide below the Street and an FY EBITDA raise smaller than the RevPAR beat implies is a real risk.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-03 a raised FY RevPAR guide, with NUG at the low end on Middle East construction delays and investment spending raised, was sold -6.97% (baseline; https://finviz.com/news/375971/marriott-shares-slip-despite-earnings-beat-as-revenue-falls-short-of-expectations). Peer on the same line this week: Hilton -2.1% on a Q4 guide dragged by the Middle East.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock is at its high with +11.8% in 20 days and only mild put skew (+2.54). That is not the shape of a market braced for a Q4 guide trimmed on the Middle East. If it were priced, the skew and the run-up would look like Hilton's after its print, not a stock 0.7% from its high.
evidence.independence: Marriott's own Q2 call (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/transcripts/MAR-2Q26-transcript) on Q4 seasonality. Accor Q3 on UAE -20% (https://www.businesstravelnewseurope.com/Accommodation/Accor-Q3-RevPAR-rises-as-Middle-East-impact-eases). Hilton commentary (https://hospitality-on.com/en/hospitality/europe-carries-hilton-third-quarter-while-middle-east-holds-back-outlook). This shares the Hilton 8-K with finding 1 but rests on a different line of it.

evidence.text: US demand stayed strong into Q4, which supports the US half of the guide. US hotel RevPAR was +5.5% in the week of 11-17 October 2026 (occupancy +3.1%, ADR +2.3%; CoStar via Hospitality Net, published 2026-10-23), after +14.2% in the week of 20-26 September on the Rosh Hashanah shift. Hyatt cited 'momentum after Labor Day' in raising its FY guide. This sits against Hilton's Q4 system guide of +3.0-3.5% and gives Marriott room for a firmer US Q4 comment than Hilton gave.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable for Marriott. Hyatt's post-Labor Day momentum comment came with a raise and +6.3% on Oct 29.
evidence.why_not_priced: These are weekly industry series that most of the Street reads, so they are largely priced. The fact is filed small because it bears directly on how Marriott frames Q4 US against Hilton's cautious +3-3.5%.
evidence.independence: Hyatt 8-K, post-Labor Day momentum (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001468174/000146817426000029/q32026earningsrelease.htm); CoStar week of 20-26 September (https://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4134703/us-hotel-results-for-week-ending-26-september). Industry proxy, not company-confirmed.

evidence.text: Setup into the print: MAR is up 11.76% in 20 days and 8.7% since the Q2 report (vs S&P +1.4%), sits 0.7% off its 52-week high, and Street EPS ($2.86) already sits above the top of the company's Q3 guide ($2.74-2.82), with a $2.92 whisper. The last time it entered a print after a run, with a guide raise in hand (2026-08-03), it fell 6.97%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline reactions: -6.97, +1.28, +8.5, +3.16, +0.23, +1.9, -5.4. Five of seven up, median |move| 3.16%; both negative reactions were 5-7% drops.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself the price. The finding is that the bar for a positive reaction has risen above the guide-top consensus, and the whisper shows it. Short interest is about 2.5% of float, so there is no short base to squeeze on a beat.
evidence.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_20d 11.76%, pct_from_52w_high -0.7) and Yahoo daily closes. Not independent of the reaction-history argument in finding 1, which is why each is sized small.

evidence.text: New Chase and American Express US co-brand card deals were expected to add about $30M of fees in H2 2026, with global card fees up in the high-30% range for 2026. This is already in the FY guide (Q2 call), and Japan yen weakness partly offsets it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The co-brand deal announcement drove a re-rating earlier in 2026 (https://rallies.ai/news/marriott-rallies-as-analysts-re-rate-stock-on-richer-credit-card-royalties-and-2026-outlook). Not visible as a print line since.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is priced: it sits inside guidance. It is filed near zero for completeness, because an upside on card fees would show up in the Q3 fee line.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview repeats the $30M (https://finviz.com/news/407878/marriotts-q3-test-can-us-momentum-and-new-card-deals-clear-a-bar-above-guidance). Same original source.

evidence.text: The owner dispute over Bonvoy economics is unresolved. 51 owners representing nearly 1,000 hotels wrote to leadership (reported by the WSJ 2026-06-16) asking for a share of card fees. On the Q2 call management cut charge-out rates about 5%, raised award-night reimbursement and added an incentive of up to 50bp of room revenue, but declined to respond formally. Further concessions or cost (the incentive sits in owned/leased and other) could show up in Q3 margins or Q4 commentary.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on this line. Owned/leased guidance has been cut twice (Earnings Whispers preview).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is known but not quantified. A number on the call for the reimbursement or incentive cost would be new. If it were priced, the Street would carry an explicit owned/leased haircut beyond the guided $175-185M.
evidence.independence: Q2 call transcript on the concessions (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/transcripts/MAR-2Q26-transcript).

evidence.text: China and APAC look soft against Marriott's FY Greater China guide of +2-3%. In Q3, IHG Greater China RevPAR was -3.3% (weather, holiday timing), Hilton Asia Pacific -0.5%, and Accor said China declined, while Hyatt Greater China was +2.1%. Marriott's Greater China is a meaningful share of international rooms, so a Q3 China print near zero and a trimmed China guide are plausible.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed as a driver of Marriott's last reactions, which turned on the US and the Middle East.
evidence.why_not_priced: Small next to the US line. If it were priced, the China guide cut would already appear in the Street's international RevPAR assumptions, which no source shows.
evidence.independence: Hilton 8-K, APAC -0.5% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001585689/000158568926000049/q32026earningsrelease.htm); Accor Q3 (https://www.businesstravelnewseurope.com/Accommodation/Accor-Q3-RevPAR-rises-as-Middle-East-impact-eases). Mixed: Hyatt +2.1%.

evidence.text: Net rooms growth was guided to the low end of 4.5-5% because of Middle East construction delays, against Hilton's 6-7% (reiterated at the midpoint 2026-10-27), and 2026 investment spending was raised to $1.25-1.35B on key money. A further NUG trim would extend the unit-growth gap to Hilton.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The NUG trim in August came with a -6.97% day, though the release-day coverage pinned that day on the revenue miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is inside what the company already guided. It is filed small because the update lands on the print.
evidence.independence: Hilton 8-K NUG 6-7% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001585689/000158568926000049/q32026earningsrelease.htm).

evidence.text: Barclays cut its Marriott target to $262 from $276, expecting soft Q3 sales and downside to Q4 outlooks.
Hilton's own stock reaction (-2.68% premarket, -2.06% close Oct 27) as a separate peer-sympathy finding.
Hyatt's FY RevPAR raise to 5.0-5.5% as a separate guidance finding.
Gulf Q4 RevPAR expected about 30% below the prior year (STR) and S&P expecting a gradual Gulf recovery from Q4.
No published Q3 RevPAR consensus for Marriott (Earnings Whispers preview, MarketBeat, Benzinga).
No October 2026 sell-side upgrade, downgrade or price-target change found. The latest dated one is Barclays' $379 target on 2026-07-21.
No October 2026 Marriott-specific corporate news beyond the Q3 date release (https://marriott.gcs-web.com/node/37666).
No September 2026 STR monthly luxury/upper-upscale or Gulf occupancy figure. CoStar pages returned 403.
No Form 4 cluster or 8-K found since the Q2 print.
Could not confirm Hilton's Oct 28 move or Citi's view (optionfinance.fr returned 403). The Hilton close-to-close was taken from Yahoo daily bars instead.
